answer: Admittance is tied to a single piece of shoreline that nobody else can share. The operator chisels an original fourteen-line sonnet into a slate tablet and cements that tablet onto one surveyed tidal ledge in a named lagoon. A registrar later arrives at an unannounced ebb and photographs the tablet against the ledge's living barnacle map; a copied tablet or a double-booked ledge is treated as the same operator and slashed. To run N identities, an attacker must compose N different sonnets, occupy N separate ledges, and complete N real low-tide inspections that one skiff cannot cover at once.
